newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: GOLF-SOUTH AFRICANS OPEN UP 13-STROKE WORLD CUP LEAD.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-SOUTH AFRICANS OPEN UP 13-STROKE WORLD CUP LEAD.

text.p: Scintillating golf from Ernie Els and Wayne Westner gave South Africa a commanding 13-stroke lead after the third day of the World Cup of Golf at the Erinvale course on Saturday.
Both took full advantage of the ideal conditions of hot weather and a gentle breeze to card seven-under-par 65's -- the lowest rounds of the tournament.
Westner, producing some sparkling iron play and a deft touch with the putter, and Els collected 16 birdies between them as South Africa closed on 410, 22-under-par for the three days.
Scotland lie in second place on 423, the United States third on 426 and Argentina, Germany and France in fourth place on 429.
South Africa, seeking their third in this tournament, now have their sights set on breaking the World Cup record for the margin of victory.
This stands at 14 shots and has been set three times by the United States -- in 1956 (Ben Hogan and Sam Snead) and in both 1994 and 1995 (Fred Couples an Davis Love III).
"It was really wonderful out there," Els said. "We had only two bogeys and 16 birdies between us and that tells it all.
"From tee to green, we played well and we also putted well. But it's still not over and we want to play well tomorrow and bring it home."
"Strangely we have matched each other round for round with our scores," Westner said. "We're following each other's lead and we're playing as a team at the moment."
South Africa began the day just one shot ahead of playing partners Scotland but they opened up a 12-shot lead by the turn with Westner collecting six birdies in an outward nine of 30 and Els four.
Although Westner dropped shots at the 10th and the 11th, he recovered with further birdies at 14 and 16 and at the last. Els gathered three more birdies coming home in 33.

Scotland, who have never won the World Cup in 41 appearances, were unable to get going during the third round until the closing holes. Both Andrew Coltart and Paul Lawrie dropped shots at the first after bunkering their approaches to the green and they eventually slipped back to nine-under for the tournament.
Coltart carded a 72 and Lawrie a 70 and were able to vault back up the leaderboard with six birdies between them over the final six holes.
Defending champions United States, looking for their 22nd win in the tournament, made some ground on the field early on. Overnight two-under-par, they improved by four shots.
British Open champion Tom Lehman and U.S. Open title-holder Steve Jones both posted rounds of two-under 70.

Germany's Alexander Cejka produced an excellent 32 on the more difficult front nine on his way to a round of 68 and, with Bernhard Langer carding a 72, Germany ended the day level with Argentina and France.
Langer was penalised two strokes for removing loose impediments using a towel on the 13th green.
